statement: Let best(T) be the maximum, over all sets S of nodes of T such that no two nodes in S are directly linked (one is the parent of the other), of the sum of the values of the nodes in S, and let best(Null) = 0. The function returns a result r and r = best(root).
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: The function returns some result r; it does not fail because of overflow, out-of-bounds access, or a panic.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a set S of nodes of root such that no two nodes in S are directly linked (one is the parent of the other) and the sum of the values of the nodes in S is exactly r.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every set S of nodes of root such that no two nodes in S are directly linked (one is the parent of the other), the sum of the values of the nodes in S is at most r.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the sum of the values of all nodes of root.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at least the value of the root node.
preconditions: root is a finite tree that is not Null, has at most 10^4 nodes, and every node value is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= best(left) + best(right), where best(T) is defined as in spec_1 and best(Null) = 0.
preconditions: root = Node(v, left, right), where left and right are finite trees, and every node value in root is an integer in [0,10^4].

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
Whenever the function returns results r1 on t1 and r2 on t2, r1 <= r2.
preconditions: t1 and t2 are finite trees with the same shape (the same positions of Null and Node), and for every corresponding node x in t1 and x' in t2, 0 <= value(x) <= value(x') <= 10^4.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r on t and a result r' on mirror(t), r = r'.
preconditions: t is a finite tree with all node values in [0,10^4], and mirror(t) is the tree obtained by recursively swapping left and right children at every node.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r on t and a result r' on t', r' = c * r.
preconditions: t and t' are finite trees with the same shape; c is an integer with c >= 0; for every corresponding node, value_t'(x) = c * value_t(x); every value in t is nonnegative; and every value in t' lies in [0,10^4].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r on t and a result r' on t', r = r'.
preconditions: t is a finite tree with all node values in [0,10^4], and t' is obtained from t by choosing a node that has a Null child and replacing that Null child with a new leaf Node(0, Null, Null).
